# CodeCrumbs

> Practical coding tutorials, tools & dev setups. 36 practical guides for developers: AI tools, coding tutorials, hosting and desk gear. Free, no login.

## Posts

- [Netlify vs Vercel vs Cloudflare Pages (2026): Which Free Tier Actually Lasts?](https://codecrumbs.pages.dev/posts/netlify-vs-vercel-vs-cloudflare-pages): Three great free hosts, three very different limit philosophies — credits, quotas and unlimited. A side-by-side based on current 2026 pricing, and how to pick in one question.
- [How to Point Your Domain to Cloudflare Pages (Step by Step)](https://codecrumbs.pages.dev/posts/point-domain-to-cloudflare-pages): You bought a domain anywhere. Here is how to serve it from Cloudflare Pages with free HTTPS, and the one setting most people forget afterwards.
- [GitHub Pages vs Cloudflare Pages in 2026: Which Free Host Fits Your Site?](https://codecrumbs.pages.dev/posts/github-pages-vs-cloudflare-pages): Both are free forever and serve static sites over HTTPS. A practical comparison of limits, deploy flow and URL behavior, plus which one to pick for a blog, docs or a portfolio.
- [Build Your Own AI Security Camera with WebRTC (Step by Step)](https://codecrumbs.pages.dev/posts/build-ai-security-camera-webrtc): Turn any IP camera into a smart camera: live WebRTC view in the browser plus AI person detection with Python, all running at home.
- [Best AI Coding Agents in 2026: Claude Code vs Codex vs Cursor vs Copilot](https://codecrumbs.pages.dev/posts/best-ai-coding-agents-2026): A plain-English comparison of the AI coding agents developers actually use in 2026: what each is good at, how they're priced, and which to pick.
- [Free AI Coding Tools for Students and Beginners (2026)](https://codecrumbs.pages.dev/posts/free-ai-coding-tools-for-students): You don't need to pay to code with AI. These free tools and student offers cover autocomplete, chat and full coding agents.
- [On-Device AI Phones Explained: What They Actually Do Without the Internet](https://codecrumbs.pages.dev/posts/on-device-ai-phones-explained): Every new phone claims 'on-device AI'. Here's what that really means, which features work offline, and whether it should affect what you buy.
- [Build Your Own Coding Agent in 100 Lines of Python](https://codecrumbs.pages.dev/posts/build-your-own-coding-agent): The agent loop demystified: a model, a tool list, and a while loop. Build one that reads files and runs commands — then understand every agent product on the market.
- [Static Site Generators in 2026: Hugo, Eleventy, Astro, Jekyll](https://codecrumbs.pages.dev/posts/static-site-generators-compared): What each generator optimizes for, who should use which, and why a fifty-line Python script can still beat all of them for a blog.
- [Best Headphones for Coding and Deep Work](https://codecrumbs.pages.dev/posts/best-headphones-for-coding): Open-back vs closed-back, ANC that actually works, and what matters when you wear headphones for eight hours straight.
